note: Hand-curated allowlist of valley bases and trailheads, read by both
tools/fetch-osm.mjs (which queries these ids directly) and
tools/build-poi.mjs (which lets them bypass the park-boundary test).
WHY AN ALLOWLIST, when huts got a simple 750 m boundary buffer instead:
there is no threshold that separates these from the noise. The wanted
791 and 1210 m outside the boundary - a continuum, with the largest interior
gap only 419 m, and it falls between Le Thumel and Gimillan, i.e. between two
places we want. Meanwhile a strict place=* filter would add 381 mostly
meaningless `locality` toponyms while still omitting Cogne itself, and the
tightest buffer that catches all 14 (1250 m) starts admitting points in the
DEM's nodata margin with fake 238.5 m elevations. So: 22 curated rows.
KEYED ON OSM ID, NEVER NAME. Three real traps found while assembling this:
Valsavarenche's road end is named 'Le Pont' in OSM, and a DIFFERENT hamlet
genuinely called 'Pont' exists in Val di Rhemes (both are listed below);
'Thumel' is 'Le Thumel'; and Eaux Rousses is mapped as 'L'Eau-Rousse'
(singular, hyphenated) - the plural spelling belongs to a bus stop node.
`name` below is the expected OSM name: fetch-osm.mjs warns if OSM no longer
matches it, so an id that gets retagged or deleted upstream is noticed
rather than silently dropped.
`displayName` overrides what the app shows, only where OSM's name would
make a place unfindable by the name people actually use.
NOT INCLUDED, deliberately: Ceresole Reale, Noasca, Locana, Rosone and
Talosio are 0.87-4.9 km SOUTH of the DEM bbox, so there is no terrain
under them. Adding them needs a new heightmap extraction
(docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 3), not a change here.

trailheads.name: Le Pont
trailheads.note: road end, start for Rifugio Vittorio Emanuele II / Gran Paradiso

trailheads.name: L'Eau-Rousse
trailheads.note: start for Rifugio Chabod; user-requested, OSM uses the singular hyphenated spelling

trailheads.name: Cretaz
trailheads.note: OSM spells it without the accent; `name` must match OSM or the drift check cries wolf forever

trailheads.name: Lillaz
trailheads.note: start for the Cascate di Lillaz

trailheads.name: Pont
trailheads.note: NOT Valsavarenche's Le Pont - a distinct hamlet with the same bare name
